title: Kener
name: kener
description: Status page with built-in monitoring: it checks your sites, APIs, ports and DNS on a schedule and shows uptime, response times, incidents and planned maintenance on a public page. Source: https://github.com/rajnandan1/kener

env.name: KENER_URL
env.label: Address you'll open it on (required)
env.description: Exactly what you'll type in the browser, port included and no slash at the end, like http://192.168.1.20:3700.

env.name: KENER_SECRET
env.label: Secret key (required)
env.description: Signs everyone's logins. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy.

env.name: KENER_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Fill in the address and secret key before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them. The address has to be exactly what you'll type in the browser, like http://192.168.1.20:3700: the port you're using, and no slash at the end. Kener refuses any form sent from another address, so if it's wrong the status page still shows but signing in or saving anything gives you Cross-site POST form submissions are forbidden. To fix it, change the address in the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Then go to /account/signin straight away, as the first person there sets up the admin account. New monitors need a type under Configuration (the service URL on its own is just a link), and only show on the public status page once you add them to it under Pages. The two sample monitors check kener.ing and load their icons from there for every visitor, so delete them when you've added your own. Settings, monitors and their history live in the kener-data volume. Docs: kener.ing/docs
